name: BPH6
question: How does prostatic urethral lift compare with transurethral resection of the prostate for symptom relief, recovery, sexual function, continence, and safety?

design.population: Sexually active men with BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms who were candidates for TURP, aged at least 50 years, with IPSS above 12, Qmax at most 15 mL/s, prostate volume at most 60 cc, and no obstructive median lobe or current urinary retention.
design.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Fig. 2; Study Protocol and Procedure, p 644

verdictNote: The 12-month composite favored PUL; symptom and flow gains favored TURP.
takeaway: Among 79 treated men analyzed, prostatic urethral lift was noninferior and superior to TURP on the 12-month BPH6 composite (23/44 [52%] vs 7/35 [20%]); TURP improved symptoms more, while lift favored recovery and ejaculatory preservation.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Sønksen J, Barber NJ, Speakman MJ, et al. "Prospective, Randomized, Multinational Study of Prostatic Urethral Lift Versus Transurethral Resection of the Prostate: 12-month Results from the BPH6 Study." *Eur Urol.* 2015;68(4):643-652. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2015.04.024
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, title and Study Endpoint and Statistical Methods, pp 643–645

results.measure: 12-month response on all six components: at least 30% IPSS reduction, recovery VAS at least 70 by 1 month, preserved erectile function and ejaculation, ISI at most 4, and no treatment-related Clavien-Dindo grade II+ event
results.note: Treated analysis: 44 PUL and 35 TURP after 91 randomized and 80 treated; noninferiority margin 10 percentage points, one-sided P less than 0.0001, then superiority P=0.005. The recovery threshold was changed from 80 to 70 and sexual-function elements to sustained assessment.
results.locator: Full text, Study Endpoint and Statistical Methods, pp 644–645; Fig. 2, p 646; Results, p 649; Table 5, p 650

results.measure: BPH6 ejaculation component: semen emission sustained during 12 months
results.note: Component comparison, not a separate primary endpoint; denominator was not stated for this component.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 645; Results, p 647; Table 5, p 650

results.measure: BPH6 recovery component: visual analogue score at least 70/100 by 1 month
results.note: The original 80/100 threshold yielded 57% versus 32%; component denominators were not stated.
results.locator: Full text, Study Endpoint and Statistical Methods, p 644; Results, p 646; Table 5, p 650

results.measure: Mean paired change from baseline at 12 months; larger reduction favors TURP
results.note: Adjusted difference is TURP minus PUL in paired change; the separate BPH6 symptom-response component was 73% versus 91% (P=0.05).
results.locator: Full text, Table 4, p 648; Table 5, p 650

harms.label: Treatment-related Clavien-Dindo events and selected adverse events through 12 months

values.exp: grade I 30/44 (68%); grade II 3/44 (7%); grade IIIb 4/44 (9%); retention 4/44 (9%); UTI 3/44 (7%); retrograde ejaculation 0/44
values.ctl: grade I 26/35 (74%); grade II 4/35 (11%); grade IIIb 5/35 (14%); retention 0/35; UTI 2/35 (6%); retrograde ejaculation 7/35 (20%)

harms.note: Grades are patient counts within each grade, not mutually exclusive totals; no grade IIIa events were reported. TURP grade IIIb events included bleeding, stricture, and secondary treatment.

harms.label: Reintervention within 12 months

values.ctl: 5/35 (14%); 2 for bleeding, 1 urethral stricture, 2 for recurrent LUTS

harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 649; Table 7, p 650
harms.note: Secondary treatment for recurrent LUTS alone was 3/44 (6.8%) versus 2/35 (5.7%); overall reintervention P=0.5.

delivery.label: Procedure and early recovery

values.exp: mean 4.7 implants (n=44); mean anesthesia time 55 min (n=44); discharge 1.0 d (n=44); return to activity 11 d (n=43); catheter >24 h in 45%
values.ctl: 12 unipolar and 23 bipolar TURPs; mean anesthesia time 71 min (n=35); discharge 1.9 d (n=35); return to activity 17 d (n=32); catheter >24 h in 74%

delivery.note: PUL used permanent lateral-lobe retraction implants; surgeon experience before enrollment was 0–20 PUL procedures versus extensive TURP experience.
